newsitem.title: ITALY: Australia pledges cash for Zaire relief.
newsitem.headline: Australia pledges cash for Zaire relief.

text.p: Australia on Thursday welcomed international steps to provide relief to starving refugees in eastern Zaire and pledged money to back up the operation.

"This morning my government announced it would provide initial assistance of 2.6 million Australian dollars to engage experienced personnel to supervise the distribution of supplies, provide necessary medical attention and coordinate relief efforts in Zaire," primary industries minister John Anderson told a U.N. food summit.

"Australia welcomes initiatives in the Security Council and on the part of countries in Central Africa to provide relief to those caught up in this conflict, and to provide peace and security in this region," he said.
But Anderson also reminded leaders at the World Food Summit that while the Zaire crisis gave the event "added poignancy," hunger was a global problem.
"It is an international tragedy, indeed I would say a cause for shame, that each night hundreds of millions of fellow human beings go to sleep hungry or malnourished," he said.
He urged governnments to give life to the words in a plan of action adopted at the outset of the summit on Wednesday, committing them to halving the number of hungry in 20 years.
"It is unacceptable that despite adequate global food production, people go hungry," Anderson said.
Supporting summit remarks by U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman on Wednesday, Anderson said speeding up free trade reforms would help countries cut food shortages.
"It is, I believe, inevitable, that the pursuit of food security through inward-looking policies based on the notion of self-sufficiency will result in costly failure," he said.
Several African governments and non-governmental organisations at the summit have attacked the current free trade era as abandoning the poor.
